h1: The 7 Best Electric Snow Shovels Under $150 for Driveways and Walks, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Electric Snow Shovels Under $150: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 cordless and corded electric snow shovels under $150, scored on clearing width, throw distance, battery runtime and handling.
summary: The Yardzpo 14 inch cordless shovel is the best for a driveway and sidewalk, with an 830W motor, two batteries and a claimed 33 foot throw. The Steelite 20V is the better balanced kit with two 4.0Ah packs, and the VOLTASK is the comfortable single-battery pick. For short runs near an outlet, the Snow Joe 324E has a headlight and costs far less to keep running.
intro: The most common disappointment with an electric snow shovel comes from expecting a snow blower. These tools are scoop-and-throw machines with a path 10 to 14 inches wide, built for light, powdery snow in the 4 to 7 inch range. They are superb for decks, steps, walkways and a short driveway, and hopeless against a plowed-in bank at the end of the drive or a foot of wet, heavy snow. Knowing that limit before you buy saves you the cost of the wrong machine.

We ranked seven electric shovels under $150 with that in mind, weighing clearing width and depth, battery capacity or cord, throw distance, weight and handle comfort. We reviewed the listings, and the figures for throw distance and snow per minute are the sellers' claims, not measurements. Two of the seven are corded and the rest are battery powered, and each type suits a different yard.

products.name: Yardzpo 14 Inch Cordless Snow Shovel with 2 Batteries
products.verdict: The widest path in the group, with an 830W copper motor, two batteries and a 33 foot throw claim.
products.description:
The Yardzpo has a 14 inch clearing width and an 830W copper motor that spins at 16,000 RPM. It ships with two batteries that together run for over 50 minutes, a 3-way discharge chute and a claimed throw of up to 33 feet. It sits at $100 to $200.

It takes first place because it clears the widest swath, which cuts the number of passes on a driveway. A 3-way discharge lets you aim snow to the left, right or forward depending on where the pile should land. Two batteries are the practical advantage, as you can swap and keep working while one charges. The throw distance is the highest claim here, though it will be shorter in wet snow.

Buy it for a one- or two-car driveway plus a sidewalk in typical snow. Keep both batteries charged, since cold weather shortens runtime.
pros: Two batteries double the work time
cons: Throw claim drops in wet snow
products.idealFor: Homeowners clearing a driveway and sidewalk after moderate snow.
products.skipIf: You face deep drifts or heavy wet snow.

products.name: Steelite 20V Cordless Electric Snow Shovel, 13 Inch
products.verdict: Two 20V 4.0Ah batteries, a 6 inch clearing depth and an adjustable chute.
products.description:
The Steelite clears a 13 inch width and 6 inches deep, runs on two 20V 4.0Ah batteries, and moves a claimed 300 lbs of snow per minute. The throw is listed as up to 23 feet, and the chute adjusts 30 degrees each way. Price is $100 to $200.

Second place goes to it because the battery capacity is clearly stated, and a pair of 4.0Ah packs is a generous amount for a shovel. The adjustable chute lets you steer snow away from a walkway, and the 6 inch depth tells you the practical limit for a single pass. It has a narrower path than the Yardzpo and a shorter claimed throw, which is why it sits behind.

Choose it if you want clear specs and a spare battery in the box. For a large driveway the extra inch of width on the Yardzpo helps.
products.idealFor: Cordless buyers who want a spare battery in the box.
products.skipIf: You want the widest path available.

products.name: VOLTASK 24V Cordless Snow Shovel, 13.2 Inch
products.verdict: A 24V 4.0Ah shovel with an ergonomic handle and about 30 minutes of continuous runtime.
products.description:
The VOLTASK has a 13.2 inch blade, a 24V 4.0Ah lithium-ion battery and about 30 minutes of continuous runtime. The throw is up to 23 feet, and the handle is designed for comfort. Expect $100 to $200 at the register.

Third place suits it because it ships with one battery, where the two above include two. Thirty minutes is enough for a sidewalk and steps but may not finish a long driveway. The comfortable handle is the draw, and a safe-start design helps avoid accidental starts. A second battery, if sold separately for this platform, would fix the main weakness.

Pick it for a sidewalk, porch and short driveway and for comfort in use. For a bigger area, choose the kits with two batteries.
cons: One battery only in the kit
products.idealFor: Users who want comfortable handling and safe starts.
products.skipIf: You need to clear a long driveway on one charge.

products.name: Pavrxeo 21V Cordless Snow Shovel, 13 Inch
products.verdict: A foldable frame and a shock-absorbing handle for back comfort and small garages.
products.description:
The Pavrxeo is a 21V cordless shovel that clears a path 12 inches wide and 7 inches deep. It has a shock-absorbing handle and a frame that collapses flat with a knob twist. Budget $50 to $100.

Fourth place reflects its focus because it is the one built for storage and comfort. The shock-absorbing handle reduces the jolt through your arms when the auger meets a patch of ice, and a foldable frame lets it hang on a garage wall. The 7 inch depth is the deepest listed here. It lacks a stated battery capacity and throw distance, so you cannot compare runtime with the others.

Buy it if garage space is tight or your back complains about vibration. Confirm the battery capacity with the seller.
products.idealFor: Small garages and users who want a back-friendly handle.
products.skipIf: You want published runtime and throw figures.

products.name: Snow Joe 324E Electric Snow Shovel with LED Headlight
products.verdict: A 10 amp corded shovel with an LED headlight, an 11 inch path and about 14 lbs of weight.
products.description:
The Snow Joe 324E has a 10 amp corded motor, an LED headlight, a claimed 300 lbs per minute and an 11 inch path. It weighs about 14 lbs and retails around $100 to $200.

Fifth place is about the cord because a cord limits where it can go, but it removes the battery question. A corded motor runs for as long as you have power, with no charge to forget and no cold-weather drop in capacity. The headlight helps with early mornings and evenings when the snow falls in the dark, and at 14 lbs it is light enough to push one-handed. You will need an outdoor-rated extension cord, and a cord can catch on the pile you are throwing.

Choose it if your walk and porch are near an outlet. For a long driveway, go cordless.
products.idealFor: Early-morning or evening shovelers who want light and no upkeep.
products.skipIf: Your driveway is far from an outlet.

products.name: Westinghouse WSnow11S 11 Inch Corded Snow Shovel
products.verdict: A 120V 10A corded shovel with an 11 inch by 6 inch path at the lowest price.
products.description:
The Westinghouse WSnow11S has a 120V 10A corded motor and clears an 11 inch wide, 6 inch deep path. It is rated for 300 lbs of snow per minute and a throw of up to 20 feet. The price band is $50 to $100.

Sixth place follows because it matches the Snow Joe on capacity and path while leaving out the headlight, and the savings are modest. The brand name is familiar for generators and power tools, which helps on support and parts. A 6 inch depth fits typical light snow, and 20 feet of throw keeps the pile out of the way.

Buy it for a small area near an outlet where the cord is no trouble. Choose the Snow Joe if you shovel in the dark.
pros: Lowest price of the corded models
products.idealFor: Small areas near an outlet where cords are no trouble.
products.skipIf: You shovel before dawn or far from power.

products.name: SKIL PWR CORE 20 10 Inch Snow Shovel Kit
products.verdict: A 10 inch kit with a 4.0Ah battery and charger, aimed at decks and patios.
products.description:
The SKIL kit has a 10 inch blade, a 20V 4.0Ah battery, a 60W charger and a claimed throw of up to 20 feet. The listing claims it can clear 3 inches of snow on a one-car driveway per charge. Price runs $100 to $200.

It finishes last because the blade is the narrowest and the driveway claim is modest, at 3 inches of snow per charge. That statement is honest, and it tells you the real use: a deck, patio, steps or a short walkway. The kit includes the battery and charger, which is complete, and the 20V platform may share batteries with other SKIL tools.

Choose it for decks, porches and a short path in light snow. Do not buy it for a long driveway.
products.idealFor: Light snow on decks, patios and walkways with a trusted brand.

methodology.title: Clearing width and depth
methodology.description: We compared the stated path width and depth, since a wider path means fewer passes and depth sets the snow level it can handle.

methodology.title: Power source and runtime
methodology.description: We weighed battery capacity, number of packs and stated runtime against corded motors that run as long as power is available.

methodology.title: Throw distance and chute
methodology.description: We looked at claimed throw and chute adjustment, which decide where the snow lands and how much you rework.

methodology.title: Weight and handling
methodology.description: We considered stated weight, handle comfort and folding designs, because a shovel you can use comfortably gets used.

methodology.title: Value and listing clarity
methodology.description: We favored kits with batteries and chargers included and listings that state their limits honestly.

whatMatters.detail: Width is the swath cleared on each pass, and depth is the thickest snow it can take in a single pass. Most electric shovels clear 10 to 14 inches wide and 6 to 7 inches deep. Check both numbers, and expect to take deeper snow in layers.

Battery capacity is measured in amp-hours, and a 4.0Ah pack gives roughly 30 minutes in light snow. Two packs let you keep working while one charges. Look for a stated runtime and note that cold weather reduces battery performance.

A corded shovel runs as long as you have power but needs an outdoor extension cord. A cordless one moves freely but is limited by the battery. Pick corded for a small area near an outlet, and cordless for driveways.
Throw is how far the snow flies from the chute, and claims run from 20 to 33 feet. Distance falls with wet or heavy snow. An adjustable chute helps you aim the pile away from where you will walk.
A shovel that weighs about 14 lbs is easy to maneuver, but heavier ones tire your arms. A shock-absorbing or ergonomic handle reduces strain. Check the weight and handle description before buying.

cards.text: A wide path, a chute you can aim, and enough runtime to finish the job. Light powder throws far, so throw distance claims are most realistic here.

faq.q: Can an electric snow shovel handle wet, heavy snow?
faq.a: It struggles. These tools work best on light, dry snow up to about 6 or 7 inches deep. For wet or deeper snow, take thin layers and slow down, or use a snow blower.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with electric snow shovels?
faq.a: Trying to clear too deep in one pass or running over gravel. The auger can jam or throw stones. Set expectations to light snow and keep the path clear of loose debris.

faq.q: Is an electric shovel worth it over a manual one?
faq.a: It is if you want less lifting. The machine does the throwing, which is easier on the back and shoulders. A manual shovel is cheaper and handles any depth, but takes more effort.

faq.q: What extension cord does a corded shovel need?
faq.a: An outdoor-rated cord of sufficient gauge for 10 amps, kept as short as practical. Check the maker's guidance for length and gauge. Always plug into a GFCI outlet.

faq.q: How should I store the batteries?
faq.a: Store packs inside the house and top them up the night before snow arrives. Cold lowers battery output, so warm a pack indoors before use. Store them partly charged over the off-season.

faq.q: Can I use it on gravel driveways?
faq.a: It is risky, since the auger can pick up stones and throw them. Leave a thin layer of snow if you must clear gravel. Raise the shovel slightly to avoid scraping the surface.

finalTake: The Yardzpo 14 Inch Cordless Snow Shovel is the best electric snow shovel under $150, thanks to its wide path and two batteries. The Steelite is the better-documented alternative, and the VOLTASK is the comfortable pick for a shorter job. For close-to-outlet jobs, the Snow Joe 324E is the most convenient corded option.
